- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above recent peak for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates mean-reversion periods; if 3–5 consecutive days show price drifting away from 30-day moving average, adjust forecast toward MA with 1–3% lag correction.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price volatility is high, reduce forecast variance by 15–25% to avoid overconfidence in short-term momentum.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative, model often fails to adjust quickly; delay forecast correction by 1–2 days and apply downward bias of 1–3% until sentiment stabilizes.
